units.title: Factor the actual precision as a positive square
units.statement: For every natural n>=3, real kappa>=4 and real orthogonal n by n matrix O, put M=(sqrt(kappa)+1)I-(sqrt(kappa)-1)O. The literal precision A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T) equals (1/4) M^T M.
assumptions: n is a natural number with n>=3, retaining the source standing block range.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n); determinant -1 and +1 are both included.
All square roots are the nonnegative real square root. No Haar law, probabilistic average or integrability premise is part of these pointwise identities.

steps.title: Expand the orthogonal square
steps.text: Write s=sqrt(kappa). Orthogonality gives O^T O=I. Expand the two factors, keeping O and O^T distinct.
steps.lean: Use mem_orthogonalGroup_iff', transpose linearity and distributivity of matrix multiplication.

steps.title: Use the nonnegative square root
steps.text: The standing kappa>=4 implies kappa>=0, so s^2=kappa. The diagonal and cross coefficients then give the exact source precision.
steps.lean: After expanding matrix entries, ring normalization and Real.sq_sqrt prove the coefficients. The existing literal singleBlockPrecision is used unchanged.

units.title: Fix the positive branch of the determinant square root
units.statement: For every natural n>=3, real kappa>=4 and real orthogonal n by n matrix O, the nonnegative real square root of det(A_O) equals 2^(-n) det((sqrt(kappa)+1)I-(sqrt(kappa)-1)O). The determinant on the right is positive; it is not replaced by an assumed absolute-value identity.
assumptions: n is a natural number with n>=3, retaining the source standing block range.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n); determinant -1 and +1 are both included.
All square roots are the nonnegative real square root. No Haar law, probabilistic average or integrability premise is part of these pointwise identities.

steps.title: Keep every matrix on the path nonsingular
steps.text: Put a=sqrt(kappa)+1 and b=sqrt(kappa)-1. Then 0<=b<a. If (aI-tO)v=0 for 0<=t<=b, orthogonality gives a^2||v||_2^2=t^2||v||_2^2. Since a^2>t^2, v=0. This proves the determinant never vanishes.
steps.lean: The private shiftedOrthogonal_det_pos derives norm preservation directly from O^T O=I, uses the finite sum of coordinate squares, and applies Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff. No invertibility/sign bound is a public binder.

steps.title: Continuity fixes the sign
steps.text: At t=0 the determinant is a^n>0. The determinant is continuous on [0,b]. If its final value were nonpositive, the intermediate value theorem would give a zero on that interval, contradicting nonsingularity.
steps.lean: Continuous.matrix_det and intermediate_value_Icc' supply the actual sign argument. The source uses a reverse-triangle norm bound for invertibility; Lean instead uses the equivalent squared-norm kernel contradiction. That quantitative norm bound is retained in the source graph and is not separately claimed as a new Lean estimate.

steps.title: Take the positive square root
steps.text: Apply determinants to the already proved factorization. Multiplicativity and transpose invariance give det(A_O)=4^(-n)(det M)^2. The candidate 2^(-n)det M is positive and its square is exactly det(A_O), fixing the real square-root branch.
steps.lean: singleBlockPrecision_factorization is genuinely consumed. Matrix.det_smul, det_mul, det_transpose and Real.sqrt_eq_iff_mul_self_eq_of_pos finish the identity.

units.title: Move the determinant sign inside the normalization factor
units.statement: For every natural n>=3, real kappa>=4 and real orthogonal n by n matrix O of either determinant sign, det(O) sqrt(det(A_O)) equals 2^(-n) det((sqrt(kappa)+1)O-(sqrt(kappa)-1)I).
assumptions: n is a natural number with n>=3, retaining the source standing block range.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n); determinant -1 and +1 are both included.
All square roots are the nonnegative real square root. No Haar law, probabilistic average or integrability premise is part of these pointwise identities.

steps.title: Multiply by the transpose inside the determinant
steps.text: The exact matrix identity O^T M=(sqrt(kappa)+1)O^T-(sqrt(kappa)-1)I follows from O^T O=I. Determinant multiplicativity and det(O^T)=det(O) bring the sign inside.
steps.lean: hmatrix proves the matrix equality from orthogonality; hdet is its determinant image, using det_mul and det_transpose.

steps.title: Transpose once more
steps.text: A determinant equals that of its transpose. Combine the preceding identity with the actual square-root theorem, leaving O rather than O^T in the final formula. This works for both determinant components.
steps.lean: The proof calls singleBlockPrecision_sqrt_det, not an assumed Gaussian normalization law or a sign-restricted orthogonal subgroup.
